## Summary
`$lastn` cannot serve 500 subjects: `ObservationService.lastN` has the documented N+1 (`TEACHING-DEFECT(perf-n+1)`), about 1,000 queries per request, and the controller accepts any number of subjects. Replace the loop with one set-based query and cap `subjects`.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | high | performance | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/service/ObservationService.java:69 | `patients.findById(subjectId)` then `findByPatientIdOrderByEffectiveDateTimeDesc(...)` inside the loop: N+1 with 2 queries per subject, ~1,000 round trips for 500 subjects | One set-based query: `WHERE patient_id IN (:ids)` with `row_number() over (partition by patient_id order by effective_date_time desc) = 1`. |
| ARC-002 | medium | performance | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/api/ObservationController.java:43 | `@RequestParam List<Long> subjects` has no maximum | Cap `subjects` at 100 per request and deduplicate ids (known defect D-03 returns duplicates); above the cap return 400 `OperationOutcome`. |
| ARC-003 | medium | performance | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/service/ObservationService.java:65 | Each subject's full observation history is loaded to keep only the first row | Select only the latest row per patient in SQL; the set-based query above does this. |

- Keep the existing `lastnReturnsMostRecentObservationPerSubject` test and add a query-count assertion (Hibernate statistics) for 1 vs 50 subjects.
